copy.tl: Kung ihahambing ang dalawang magkaparehong kuwerdas, ang mas maikli ay laging mas mataas ang tunog, at ang mas mahaba ay mas mababa. Ganito nakabubuo ng iba't ibang nota!
copy.bis: Kung itandi ang duha ka pareho nga kuwerdas, ang mas mubo kanunay mas taas ang tingog, ug ang mas taas mas ubos. Mao kini ang makahimo ug lain-laing nota!

What happens during the December solstice in the Northern Hemisphere?

It has the shortest day and longest night around December 21!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa December solstice sa Northern Hemisphere?

Ito ang may pinakamaikling araw at pinakamahabang gabi mga Disyembre 21!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa December solstice sa Northern Hemisphere?

Kini maoy adunay kinamub-ang adlaw ug kinatas-ang gabii mga Disyembre 21!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: smaller animals usually have faster metabolisms

copy.en:
Why do tiny animals move so fast?

In nature, smaller animals usually have faster metabolisms — elephants burn energy slowly, but a tiny shrew burns it super fast!
copy.tl:
Bakit napakabilis ng maliliit na hayop?

Sa kalikasan, kadalasang mas mabilis ang metabolismo ng mas maliit na hayop — mabagal magsunog ng enerhiya ang elepante, pero napakabilis naman ng maliit na shrew!
copy.bis:
Ngano paspas kaayo ang gagmayng mananap?

Sa kinaiyahan, kasagaran mas paspas ang metabolism sa mas gamayng mananap — hinay mosunog og kusog ang elepante, apan paspas kaayo ang gamayng shrew!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A shrimp uses its long feelers, called antennae, to sense and smell what's around it in the water.

copy.en: A shrimp uses its long feelers, called antennae, to sense and smell what's around it in the water.

copy.bis: Gigamit sa hipon ang taas nga sungot o antenna niini aron mobati ug makasimhot sa palibot sulod sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It wears a hard shell outside called an exoskeleton, protecting its soft body like armor.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (exoskeleton) but not the specific parts named in the competency (head, legs, wings) and its role is protection, not movement or gathering food.

copy.en:
Why is a shrimp's outside so hard?

It wears a hard shell outside called an exoskeleton, protecting its soft body like armor.
copy.tl:
Bakit matigas ang labas ng hipon?

May matigas na balat ito sa labas na tinatawag na exoskeleton, na parang armor na nagsisilbing panangga sa malambot nitong katawan.
copy.bis:
Nganong gahi ang gawas sa hipon?

Adunay gahi nga panit sa gawas nga gitawag exoskeleton, sama sa armor nga nagpanalipod sa humok nga lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: letting it see to both sides at the exact same time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (eyes) and its function (seeing), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of body parts to move and to gather food. Seeing is not moving or gathering food, so the card does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A shrimp's two eyes sit on little stalks that stick out, letting it see to both sides at the exact same time!
copy.tl: May dalawang matang nakatusok sa maliliit na tangkay ang hipon, kaya kaya nitong makakita sa magkabilang gilid nang sabay!
copy.bis: Ang hipon adunay duha ka mata nga nagtindog sa gagmay nga tangkay, busa makakita kini sa duha ka kilid dungan!

assignedReviews.reason: One produce example is not grow, respond, and reproduce as general living-thing characteristics.

copy.en: A chili plant can produce peppers many times over several months — you don't need to replant right away because it just keeps giving chilies.
copy.tl: Ang halaman ng siling haba ay nagbubunga nang maraming beses sa loob ng ilang buwan — hindi mo kailangang magtanim ulit agad dahil patuloy itong nagbibigay ng sili.
copy.bis: Ang tanom sa siling haba makahatag og sili sa makadaghan sulod sa pipila ka bulan — dili kinahanglan magtanom dayon pag-usab kay padayon kining mohatag og sili.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Long green chili turns red as it ripens on the plant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fruit ripening, a maturation process, but does not explicitly teach the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It only provides an example of a plant change, not the general concept or the other characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Long green chili turns red as it ripens on the plant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants from seed to mature plant. The card only mentions a chili fruit ripening on the plant; it does not describe a life cycle, stages, or comparison. It is a single observation of ripening, not a life-cycle comparison.

copy.en: Long green chili turns red as it ripens on the plant, and it tastes a bit sweeter and spicier once red.
copy.tl: Ang siling haba ay unti-unting nagiging pula habang humihinog sa halaman, at mas matamis-anghang ang lasa nito kapag pula na.
copy.bis: Ang siling haba hinay-hinay nga mahimong pula samtang mahinog sa tanom, ug mas tam-is-hait ang lami niini kung pula na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some farmers raise silkworms and grow mulberry trees to produce silk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions silkworms and mulberry trees but does not explain how they depend on each other or on the environment to meet basic needs. It only states that farmers raise them for silk production, which is a production fact, not an interdependence explanation.

copy.en: In the Philippines, some farmers raise silkworms and grow mulberry trees to produce silk.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, may mga magsasaka na nag-aalaga ng silkworm at nagtatanim ng mulberry para gumawa ng seda.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, adunay mga mag-uuma nga nag-atiman og silkworm ug nagtanom og mulberry aron makahimo og seda.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silk thread comes from the cocoon spun by a silkworm!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that silk thread comes from a silkworm's cocoon. It does not use a flow chart, does not compare life-cycle stages, and provides no information about the stages of an animal's life cycle. The cocoon is a life-cycle-related concept, but the card does not directly support the competency's requirement to compare stages using flow charts.

copy.en:
Where does silk thread come from?

Silk thread comes from the cocoon spun by a silkworm!
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang sinulid na seda?

Ang sinulid na seda ay nagmumula sa cocoon na ginagawa ng silkworm!
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang hilo nga seda?

Ang hilo nga seda gikan sa cocoon nga gihimo sa silkworm!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silk is made of protein, the same material found in our hair and nails!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses silk's composition (protein) and that it is a natural fiber, but does not describe physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silk is made of protein, the same material found in our hair and nails!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify objects at home and in the classroom as solid, liquid or gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify silk as a solid, liquid, or gas, nor does it classify any object by state of matter. It only mentions a material's composition, which is not the focus of this competency.

copy.en:
What is silk made of?

Silk is made of protein, the same material found in our hair and nails! That is why it is a natural fiber and not plastic.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gawa sa sutla?

Ang sutla ay gawa sa protina, na siyang parehong sangkap sa buhok at kuko natin! Kaya ito ay isang natural na hibla, hindi plastik.
copy.bis:
Unsay hinimo sa sutla?

Ang sutla hinimo gikan sa protina, ang samang sangkap sa atong buhok ug kuko! Mao nga natural kini nga hibla, dili plastik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The silkworm munches on mulberry leaves almost all day long!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a fact about what a silkworm eats (mulberry leaves), which is plant material. This could be used as an example when grouping animals as herbivores, but the card does not itself group animals or introduce the categories herbivore/carnivore/omnivore. It only supplies background information about one animal's diet, so it supports the competency indirectly rather than teaching the grouping skill.

copy.en: The silkworm munches on mulberry leaves almost all day long!
copy.tl: Kumakain ang silkworm ng mga dahon ng mulberry halos buong araw!
copy.bis: Mokaon ang silkworm og mga dahon sa mulberry halos tibuok adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The tiny sinarapan fish lives only in two lakes — Lake Buhi and Lake Bato in Camarines Sur, in the Bicol region.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single Philippine fish and its aquatic habitat, but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify animals/plants by habitat, nor does it provide a classification of multiple organisms. It only offers a fact about one species, which is related vocabulary but does not directly support the competency's classification skill.

copy.en: The tiny sinarapan fish lives only in two lakes — Lake Buhi and Lake Bato in Camarines Sur, in the Bicol region.
copy.tl: Matatagpuan lamang ang sinarapan sa Lake Buhi at Lake Bato sa Camarines Sur, sa rehiyon ng Bicol.
copy.bis: Ang sinarapan makit-an lang sa Lake Buhi ug Lake Bato sa Camarines Sur, sa rehiyon sa Bicol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: surface tension pulls it up into a tiny crown shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a water drop splash and surface tension, but does not describe the shape and volume properties of liquids (no definite shape, definite volume) or contrast solids/liquids/gases. Surface tension is a liquid property but not the shape/volume distinction required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a water drop hits a pool
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water as a liquid but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or their existence. It only illustrates a single liquid phenomenon, so it does not directly support identifying that matter exists in three states.

copy.en: When a water drop hits a pool, surface tension pulls it up into a tiny crown shape! Then it sinks back and breaks into smaller droplets.
copy.tl: Kapag pumatak ang tubig sa lawa, hinihila ito pataas ng surface tension sa hugis-korona! Pagkatapos, lumulubog ito pabalik at nagiging maliliit na patak.
copy.bis: Kung matagak ang tubig sa linaw, gibira kini pataas sa surface tension ngadto sa porma-korona! Dayon molugdang kini pag-usab ug mabuak ngadto sa gagmay nga tulo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sinkhole can open suddenly and become dangerous if buildings or roads sit above it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: A sinkhole is a landform, but the card does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water or describe how they influence living and non-living components as required by G5-E-1. It only warns about sudden danger to buildings/roads.

copy.en: Watch out! A sinkhole can open suddenly and become dangerous if buildings or roads sit above it.
copy.tl: Mag-ingat! Maaaring biglang bumukas ang sinkhole at maging delikado kapag may gusali o kalsada sa ibabaw nito.
copy.bis: Pag-amping! Ang sinkhole mahimong moabli nga kalit ug delikado kon adunay building o dalan sa ibabaw niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: as long as that end is lower than the source
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a siphon moving water, which implicitly relies on gravity, but it does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or explain how gravity affects materials/objects in predictable ways. The content is about fluid flow, not the force itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: as long as that end is lower than the source
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that water flows when the outlet is lower, which is a gravity-driven effect, but it does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. It focuses on the siphon mechanism rather than gravity's role.

copy.en:
How does a siphon move water through a tube?

A siphon moves water up the tube and out the other end, as long as that end is lower than the source!
copy.tl:
Paano nagpapadaloy ang siphon ng tubig sa loob ng tubo?

Inilipat ng siphon ang tubig pataas sa tubo at lumalabas sa kabilang dulo, basta't mas mababa iyon kaysa sa pinagmulan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpadagayday sa siphon og tubig sulod sa tubo?

Gibalhin sa siphon ang tubig paingon sa taas sa tubo ug mogawas sa pikas tumoy, basta mas ubos kini kay sa gigikanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The whole framework of your body's 206 bones is called the skeleton.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines the skeleton as the framework of 206 bones. It does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection, blood cell production), which is the action required by G4-L-1. The definition is useful background but does not directly teach the system's function.

copy.en:
What do we call all 206 bones together?

The whole framework of your body's 206 bones is called the skeleton.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa 206 na buto ng katawan?

Ang buong balangkas ng 206 na buto ng katawan ay tinatawag na skeleton o kalansay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tawag sa 206 ka bukog sa lawas?

Ang tibuok bayanan sa 206 ka bukog sa lawas gitawag og skeleton o kalansay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the skull is actually several bones tightly joined together, not just one.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a structural fact about the skull (multiple fused bones) but does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection). It shares the skeletal-system topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's action of describing how the system works.

copy.en:
Is the skull just one bone?

No — the skull is actually several bones tightly joined together, not just one.
copy.tl:
Iisang buto lang ba ang bungo?

Hindi — ang bungo ay binubuo ng ilang butong magkakadikit nang mahigpit, hindi iisa lamang.
copy.bis:
Usa ra ba ka bukog ang bagol?

Dili — ang bagol gilangkoban sa pipila ka bukog nga hugot nga nagdugtong, dili usa ra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: weighing collected trash is measuring
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions measuring as a science process skill but does not identify or use any specific units (mg, g, kg, °C). It does not directly support the competency's focus on units.

copy.en:
How can cleaning up show science process skills?

Going around to spot trash is observing, sorting waste is classifying, weighing collected trash is measuring, and taking photos is communicating!
copy.tl:
Paano naipapakita ng paglilinis ang science process skills?

Ang pag-ikot para makita ang basura ay observing, ang paghihiwalay ng basura ay classifying, ang pagtimbang ng nakolektang basura ay measuring, at ang pagkuha ng litrato ay communicating!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpakita sa pagpanglimpyo ang science process skills?

Ang paglibot aron makita ang basura mao ang observing, ang paglain sa basura mao ang classifying, ang pagtimbang sa nakolektang basura mao ang measuring, ug ang pagkuha og litrato mao ang communicating!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The outer surface of your skin is actually made of dead cells that slowly flake off and get replaced with new ones!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cell replacement but does not mention mitosis, meiosis, or cell division. It does not directly support recognizing the two types of cell division or describing mitosis as growth and repair.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The outer surface of your skin is actually made of dead cells that slowly flake off and get replaced with new ones!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use proper techniques in observing and identifying the parts of a cell with a microscope such as the cell membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, and chloroplasts
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about skin cells and replacement, not about using a microscope to observe and identify cell parts such as membrane, nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, or chloroplasts. No microscope techniques or cell organelles are addressed.

copy.en: The outer surface of your skin is actually made of dead cells that slowly flake off and get replaced with new ones!
copy.tl: Ang pinakalabas na bahagi ng iyong balat ay gawa pala sa mga patay na selula na unti-unting natutuklap at napapalitan ng bago!
copy.bis: Ang pinakagawas nga bahin sa imong panit hinimo diay sa mga patay nga selula nga hinay-hinay nga mangahulog ug pulihan og bag-o!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your skin is your body's first line of defense
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes skin as a barrier against germs, which is an outer body part but does not address the competency's focus on head, legs, or wings and their roles in movement and gathering food. It shares the broad topic of outer body parts but provides no direct instructional support for the stated skill.

copy.en: Your skin is your body's first line of defense — it keeps most germs from ever getting inside.
copy.tl: Ang balat ang unang harang ng katawan — pinipigilan nito ang karamihan ng germ na makapasok.
copy.bis: Ang panit mao ang unang babag sa lawas — gipugngan niini ang kadaghanan sa mga kagaw nga mosulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cold isn't the only cause — fear, excitement, or a moving song or story can give you goosebumps too.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses emotional triggers for goosebumps, not homeostasis, body system balance, or its indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). It is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cold isn't the only cause — fear, excitement, or a moving song or story can give you goosebumps too.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a body response to stimuli, which touches on responding, but it does not teach the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a general concept. It only provides a narrow example of a response without explaining the characteristic itself.

copy.en:
What else gives you goosebumps?

Cold isn't the only cause — fear, excitement, or a moving song or story can give you goosebumps too. That's why a scary story can make you shiver even on a warm day!
copy.tl:
Ano pa nagbibigay ng goosebumps?

Hindi lang lamig ang dahilan — pwede ka ring kilabutan dahil sa takot, kaba, o isang nakakaantig na kanta o kwento. Kaya minsan nangingikil ka sa nakakatakot na kwento kahit hindi malamig!
copy.bis:
Unsa pay makahatag og goosebumps?

Dili lang katugnaw ang hinungdan — mahimo ka usab makakibabot tungod sa kahadlok, kakulba, o makapatandog nga kanta o sugilanon. Mao nga usahay magkibabot ka sa makahahadlok nga sugilanon bisan dili tugnaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: blood quickly forms a scab to cover it, while new skin grows underneath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: A scab covering a cut is skin healing, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: blood quickly forms a scab to cover it, while new skin grows underneath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Skin healing is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en: Your body is a great healer! When you get a small cut, blood quickly forms a scab to cover it, while new skin grows underneath until it's fully healed.
copy.tl: Magaling gumaling ang katawan mo! Kapag may sugat, mabilis na bumubuo ang dugo ng langib bilang takip, habang gumagawa naman ng bagong balat sa ilalim hanggang tuluyang gumaling.
copy.bis: Maayo kaayo mo-ayo ang imong lawas! Kung adunay samad, dali nga mohimo ang dugo og kugan nga tabon, samtang ang bag-ong panit magtubo sa ilawom hangtod maayo na gyud.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your skin keeps water inside your body so you don't dry out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single example of water retention by the skin, which is a homeostatic function, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or mention the indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure) required by the competency. It only touches on the broad concept of maintaining internal balance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your skin keeps water inside your body so you don't dry out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency covers the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The skin is not one of these systems, and the card does not describe how any of the listed systems work. The skin's water-retention function is unrelated to the specified body systems.

copy.en: Your skin keeps water inside your body so you don't dry out.
copy.tl: Ang balat mo ay pumipigil sa tubig na lumabas sa katawan para hindi ka matuyo.

Sometimes, after danger has passed, a skink comes back and eats its own dropped tail — normal for them, since it helps recover the fat and energy stored inside that would otherwise go to waste.

Bakit binabalikan ng skink ang sarili niyang buntot?

Minsan, pagkawala ng panganib, babalik ang skink at kakainin ang sarili niyang nahulog na buntot — normal ito para sa kanila, dahil nababawi nila ang taba at enerhiyang nakaimbak doon kung hindi ay masasayang lang.

Nganong balikan sa skink ang kaugalingon niyang ikog?

Usahay, human mawala ang katalagman, mobalik ang skink ug kaonon ang iyang kaugalingong nahulog nga ikog — normal ra kini para nila, kay mabawi nila ang tambok ug enerhiya nga natipig didto nga kon dili ikasayang lang.

How many bones make up your skull?

22! Your skull is actually made up of 22 different bones.

22! Binubuo ang bungo (skull) ng tao ng 22 na buto.

22! Ang bungo (skull) sa tawo gilangkuban og 22 ka bukog.

copy.bis: Kon kulang sa tulog, mohinay ang reaksyon sa lawas mao nga mas dali ta masayop o mapandol. Mao nga ang igong tulog motabang nato nga magmaalerto ug luwas.

Ang slug at maraming kuhol ay may apat na sungot — dalawa para makakita, dalawa para makahipo!

Makahimog dako nga crater ug mopagawas ug energy nga makamugna ug kusog nga shockwaves ug firestorms, nga moguba sa tanang duol.

Ito ay ang Wolffia! Ang lumulutang na halamang ito sa tubig ay kasing liit lang ng isang butil ng buhangin.

Unsay pinakagamay nga namulak nga tanom sa kalibotan?

Mao kini ang Wolffia! Kining naglutaw nga tanom sa tubig sama lang kagamay sa usa ka lugas sa balas.

Sa pagtitinapa, ang usok ay nagpapatuyo sa isda at tumutulong patayin ang mga mikrobyo para tumagal ito!

Unsaon pagtinapa sa isda aron modugay kini?

Sa pagtinapa sa isda, ang aso magpauga niini ug motabang pagpatay sa mikrobyo aron modugay kini!

copy.bis: Ang kuhol adunay kusgan nga unod sulod sa iyang kabhang — kon mag-igtin kini, molihok kini sama sa spring nga mobira sa lawas balik sulod sa kabhang.

copy.en:
Why does a snail hide in its shell?

A snail also pulls into its shell to stop losing water, not just to hide from enemies. Its body is soft and moist, so it needs protecting.
copy.tl:
Bakit pumapasok ang kuhol sa shell nito?

Pumapasok din ito sa shell para hindi mawalan ng tubig, hindi lang para magtago sa kaaway. Malambot at basa kasi ang katawan nito.
copy.bis:
Ngano musulod ang kuhol sa iyang kabhang?

Musulod usab kini sa kabhang aron dili mawad-an og tubig, dili lang para mutago sa kaaway. Humok ug basa man gud ang iyang lawas.

copy.tl: Ang kuhol sa lupa ay malambot na hayop na may matigas na pasikot-sikot na bahay sa likod, at gumagapang ito nang mabagal habang nag-iiwan ng makintab na uhog.
copy.bis: Ang kuhol sa yuta usa ka humok nga hayop nga may gahi nga liko-liko nga balay sa likod, ug nagkamang kini og hinay samtang nagbilin og masinaw nga uhog.

copy.tl: Ang kuhol ay nag-iiwan ng makintab na bakas ng uhog habang ito ay gumagapang.
copy.bis: Ang kuhol magbilin ug sinaw nga agi sa uhog samtang kini magkamang.

copy.en:
How slow does a snail crawl?

A snail crawls at only about 0.05 kilometers per hour — that's incredibly slow!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabagal gumapang ang kuhol?

Ang kuhol ay gumagapang lamang nang halos 0.05 kilometro kada oras — napakabagal!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka hinay mokamang ang kuhol?

Ang kuhol mokamang lang ug halos 0.05 kilometro kada oras — hinay kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Snakes are cold-blooded and can't warm themselves without outside heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why snakes are absent from snowy places due to being cold-blooded, but it does not describe how animals have changed/adapted to suit their environment (e.g., mimicry or camouflage). It is only tangentially about animals and their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: that's why so many live in warm countries like the Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions snakes living in warm countries like the Philippines, but it does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial), nor does it teach that classification.

copy.en:
Why are there no snakes where it snows?

Snakes are cold-blooded and can't warm themselves without outside heat, so they'd freeze in snowy places — that's why so many live in warm countries like the Philippines!
copy.tl:
Bakit halos walang ahas kung saan may niyebe?

Dahil cold-blooded ang mga ahas, hindi nila kayang painitin ang sarili kung walang init sa paligid, kaya mamamatay sila sa lamig — kaya marami silang nakatira sa mainit na lugar tulad ng Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Nganong halos walay bitin kung diin naay snow?

Tungod kay cold-blooded ang mga bitin, dili nila mapainit ang kaugalingon kon walay init sa palibot, mao nga mamatay sila sa katugnaw — mao nga daghan kanila nagpuyo sa init nga dapit sama sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It moves back and forth -- into the sun when cold, into the shade when hot -- to stay just right.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a snake's behavioral thermoregulation (shuttling between sun and shade). G5-L-9 asks for examples of how animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. The card does not describe evolutionary change or adaptation of the kind exemplified; it only shows an immediate behavior for heat control, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does a snake control its body heat?

A snake has no built-in thermostat! It moves back and forth -- into the sun when cold, into the shade when hot -- to stay just right.
copy.tl:
Paano kinokontrol ng ahas ang init ng katawan?

Walang thermostat ang ahas! Balik-balik itong lumilipat -- lalabas sa araw kapag malamig, papasok sa lilim kapag mainit -- para manatili sa tamang init.
copy.bis:
Unsaon sa bitin pagkontrol sa iyang kainit?

Walay thermostat ang bitin! Balik-balik kining mobalhin -- mogawas sa adlaw kon mobugnaw, mosulod sa landong kon moinit -- aron magpabilin sa sakto nga kainit.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (the eye cap) but does not identify its role in movement or gathering food, which is the specific action of the competency.

copy.en:
Does a snake have eyelids?

A snake has no eyelids at all — instead, a clear cap covers each eye, and it sheds off along with the skin!
copy.tl:
May talukap ba ng mata ang ahas?

Walang talukap ang mata ng ahas — sa halip, may malinaw na takip ito na natatanggal din kasabay ng balat!
copy.bis:
Naa bay pilok ang mata sa halas?

Ang halas walay pilok sa mata — hinuon, naay tin-aw nga tabon ang matag mata nga matangtang usab kuyog sa panit!

copy.bis: Ang bar soap gihimo gamit ang sodium hydroxide (NaOH), samtang ang liquid soap gamit ang potassium hydroxide (KOH). Ang kalainan sa lye ang nagdetermina kung solid o likido!

copy.tl: Pagkatapos magluto, dumidikit ang mantika sa kawali at plato. Hinihati at binabalot ng sabong panghugas-pinggan ang makapal na grasa, kaya nadudulas ito pag-banlawan — kahit langis na hindi tinatablan ng tubig!
copy.bis: Human magluto, mopilit ang mantika sa kawa ug plato. Gibahinon ug giputos sa sabong panghugas-plato ang baga nga grasa, busa modanlog kon banlawan — bisan lana nga dili matandog sa tubig!

copy.en: Soap weakens water's surface tension, letting water spread into dirt more easily so it can wash things clean!
copy.tl: Pinahihina ng sabon ang surface tension ng tubig, kaya mas madaling makapasok ang tubig sa dumi para malabhan ito!
copy.bis: Nagpaluya ang sabon sa surface tension sa tubig, mao nga mas sayon makasulod ang tubig sa hugaw aron mahugasan kini!

Why can't plain water wash off greasy hands?

Water just slides over oil — the two don't mix! Soap breaks up the grease and grabs it, which is why water alone can't clean a greasy plate.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi kayang linisin ng tubig lang ang mamantikang kamay?

Dumudulas lang ang tubig sa langis — hindi sila nag-hahalo! Hinihati at hinahawakan ng sabon ang mantika, kaya hindi kayang linisin ng tubig lang ang mamantikang pinggan.
copy.bis:
Ngano dili makahimo ang tubig lang paglimpyo sa mantikaon nga kamot?

Modagan lang ang tubig sa lana — dili sila magsagol! Gibahinon ug gikuptan sa sabon ang mantika, mao nga dili makahimo ang tubig lang paglimpyo sa mantikaon nga plato.

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how soap emulsifies oil so water can rinse it away, which is about cleaning/emulsification, not any of the listed separation techniques (decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, using magnets). It shares the broad topic of mixtures but does not demonstrate or support the specific competency.

copy.en:
How does the water finally wash away the oily dirt?

Because the soap has wrapped up the oil, the water can now rinse it all away!
copy.tl:
Paano naaanod ng tubig ang mamantikang dumi?

Dahil nababalot na ng sabon ang langis, naaanod na ito ng tubig kapag binanlawan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghugas sa tubig sa lanahon nga hugaw?

Tungod kay naputos na sa sabon ang lana, mahugasan na kini sa tubig kung banlawan!

copy.en:
Ever wonder how soap bubbles trap dirt and grease to keep you clean?

Soap lather is a foam where soap molecules coat air bubbles and lower water surface tension. This foam helps carry away dirt and grease!
copy.tl:
Paano kaya nakakalinis ang bula ng sabon sa pamamagitan ng pagkuha ng dumi?

Ang bula ng sabon ay isang foam kung saan ang soap molecules ay nagbabalot sa air bubbles at nagpapababa ng surface tension ng tubig para madaling makuha ang dumi!
copy.bis:
Giunsa man paglimpyo sa bula sa sabon pinaagi sa pagkuha sa dumi ug grease?

Ang bula sa sabon usa ka foam diin ang soap molecules nagbalot sa air bubbles ug nagpababa sa surface tension sa tubig aron makuha ang dumi ug grease!

copy.en: Making soap also produces glycerin! Glycerin helps keep your skin moist and soft, which is why it is sometimes left inside the soap to help you.
copy.tl: Sa paggawa ng sabon, nabubuo rin ang glycerin! Nakakatulong ang glycerin na panatilihing basa at malambot ang balat, kaya minsan iniiwan ito sa loob ng sabon.
copy.bis: Pagkahimo sa sabon, mahimo usab ang glycerin! Makatabang ang glycerin nga magpabilin nga umog ug humok ang panit, mao nga usahay ibilin kini sa sulod sa sabon.

copy.en: Plain water cannot remove oily dirt because water and oil do not mix! We need soap to make them get along so the oil washes away.
copy.tl: Hindi natatanggal ng tubig lang ang malangis na dumi dahil ayaw maghalo ng tubig at langis! Kailangan natin ng sabon para magkasundo sila at matanggal ang dumi.
copy.bis: Ang tubig lang dili makakuha sa malangis nga hugaw kay dili magsagol ang tubig ug lana! Kinahanglan ta og sabon aron magkasinabot sila ug makuha ang hugaw.

copy.tl: Kailangan ng mas maraming sabon sa matigas na tubig! Nasasayang ang unang bahagi sa pakikipagsama sa mineral bago mabulain.
copy.bis: Nagkinahanglan og daghang sabon ang gahi nga tubig! Mausik ang unang bahin sa pagsagol sa mineral una pa mabula.

copy.tl: Kapag humukay ka malalim sa lupa, makikita mo na nakapatong-patong pala ito sa iba't ibang magagandang antas!
copy.bis: Kung kalutan nimo ang yuta, makita nimo nga nagkapatong-patong pala kini sa nagkalainlaing ang-ang!

Do solar panels work perfectly all the time?

Solar panels make less electricity on cloudy days and absolutely none at night!
copy.tl:
Gumagana ba nang perpekto ang solar panel sa lahat ng oras?

Gumagawa ng mas kaunting kuryente ang solar panel kapag maulap, at wala itong ginagawa kapag gabi!
copy.bis:
Naggana ba og perpekto ang solar panel sa tanang oras?

Naghimo ug gamay nga koryente ang solar panel kon mapanganod, ug wala gyud kon gabii!

Unsaon paghimo og kuryente sa solar panel?

How many planets orbit the Sun in our solar system?

There are exactly eight planets that orbit the Sun in our amazing solar system!
copy.tl:
Ilang planeta ang umiikot sa Araw sa ating sistemang solar?

May walong planeta na umiikot sa Araw sa ating nakamamanghang sistemang solar!

Pila ka planeta ang naglibot sa Adlaw sa atong sistemang solar?

Adunay walo ka planeta nga naglibot sa Adlaw sa atong katingad-an nga sistemang solar!

copy.en:
Is glass really a liquid?

Not all solids have a crystalline structure! Glass is an amorphous solid with irregular atoms, unlike a crystal. Some call it a 'supercooled liquid,' but it's truly a solid!
copy.tl:
Likido ba talaga ang salamin?

Hindi lahat ng solido ay may crystalline structure! Ang salamin ay isang amorphous solid na may di-regular na atoms, hindi tulad ng kristal. Minsan itong tawaging 'supercooled liquid,' pero solid talaga ito!
copy.bis:
Likido ba gyud ang salamin?

Dili tanan nga solido adunay crystalline structure! Ang salamin usa ka amorphous solid nga may di-regular nga atoms, dili sama sa kristal. Minsan kini gitawag og 'supercooled liquid,' pero tinuod kini nga solid!

Pila ka solstice ang naa sa usa ka tuig?

Adunay duha (2) ka solstice matag tuig: ang June solstice ug ang December solstice.

When does a super loud sonic boom happen in the sky?

A sonic boom happens when an aircraft goes faster than the speed of sound (Mach 1, about 343 m/s in air)!

Kailan nangyayari ang isang napakalakas na sonic boom sa kalangitan?

Ang sonic boom ay nangyayari kapag ang isang eroplano ay lumampas sa bilis ng tunog (Mach 1, mga 343 m/s sa hangin)!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mahitabo ang kusog kaayo nga sonic boom sa kahanginan?

Ang sonic boom mahitabo kung ang eroplano molabaw sa katulin sa tingog (Mach 1, mga 343 m/s sa hangin)!

copy.en: An anechoic chamber is a special room lined with pointed foam that absorbs almost all sound! Engineers use it to test equipment without echo interference.
copy.tl: Ang anechoic chamber ay silid na puno ng matutulis na foam na sumasipsip ng halos lahat ng tunog! Ginagamit ito ng mga inhinyero para subukan ang kagamitan nang walang echo interference.
copy.bis: Ang anechoic chamber usa ka espesyal nga kwarto nga puno sa tinudhong foam nga nagsipsip sa halos tanan nga tunog! Gigamit sa mga inhinyero sa pagsulay sa mga kagamitan nga walay echo interference.

Who was the first person to do a spacewalk, and what happened during his trip?

Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov! In March 1965, his 12-minute spacewalk had a serious problem when his spacesuit ballooned outward.

Sino ang unang tao na nag-spacewalk, at ano ang nangyari sa kanyang biyahe?

Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov! Noong Marso 1965, ang kanyang 12-minutong spacewalk ay nagkaproblema nang lumaki at magsabog ang kanyang spacesuit.

Kinsa ang unang tawo nga ni-spacewalk, ug unsay nahitabo sa iyang biyahe?

Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov! Niadtong Marso 1965, ang iyang 12-minutong spacewalk nagkaproblema sa dihang nagsabog sa gawas ang iyang spacesuit.
